title: Pocketed Reserve Lanes: modular reserved GPU lanes + burst handshake pricing and contract ops proposal
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Proposal for a modular reserved GPU packaging approach called 'Pocketed Reserve Lanes' (PRL). PRL breaks a customer's committed capacity into smaller named pockets (lanes) that can be priced and contracted independently, with a controlled burst handshake mechanism to use adjacent unused pockets and a preemptible helper pool for short-term surge. Goal: increase attractiveness of reserved capacity to mid-market / enterprise customers who need predictable baseline throughput but want flexible burst and predictable overage economics. This ticket captures pricing experiments, contract language drafts for SLAs/credits, implementation guardrails, and the security/Q&A items needed for enterprise procurement.
background: Problem: Customers find large monolithic GPU commitments inflexible. They want smaller guaranteed throughput bands aligned to features (e.g., embed lane for search, gen lane for UI, batch lane for offline), predictable pricing for burst, and clear contract terms for credits/overage. Sales teams also report friction in enterprise negotiations over preemption and burst guarantees. Previous PM work focused on slab and burst credits; this initiative is a modular approach aimed at higher conversion for 50-500k ARR customers.
proposal: 1) Product construct: Each PRL purchase contains N lanes (e.g., 4 x small lanes or 1 x large + 2 x small) where each lane is a named reserved throughput allocation (vGPU-equivalent or p99 qps target). 2) Burst handshake: When a lane is underutilized and another lane requests extra capacity, traffic can 'handshake' and temporarily borrow up to X% of adjacent lane capacity for up to Y minutes. 3) Helper pool (preemptible): Introduce an optional discounted helper pool for short bursts with preemption + best-effort availability. 4) Credit model: Overages are charged via burnable burst credits at tiered rates; unused burst credits expire quarterly (or can be converted into future month discount under contract). 5) SLA tiers: Bronze / Silver / Gold mapped to p99 latency targets, throughput guarantees, and monthly uptime SLA. Contract language includes service credits, make-whole clauses for sustained latency SLO misses, and explicit preemption & eviction rules for helper pool. 6) Ops controls: Allow purchase-time autoscale cushions and optional regional fallbacks. 7) Reporting: Console surfaces lane-level utilization, real-time handshake events, credit burn history, and predicted burn curve.
acceptance_criteria: Define SKU table for 3 lane sizes with per-lane price and burst-rate multipliers
Legal-approved contract language for burst handshake, helper pool preemption, and credits
Engineering implementation plan with API changes, quota model, and billing hooks (ENG-55123 assigned)
Console prototypes for lane-level dashboards (DES-3390 assigned)
Pilot with at least two enterprise customers (Nimbus AI, HelixSearch) and measurable improvement in conversion / NRR for dedicated offers
tasks: Finalize internal SKU matrix and pricing tiers
Run two A/B pricing experiments (A: higher baseline discount + limited burst; B: lower discount + generous burst credits)
Draft contract addendum and sample SOW language for legal and sales
Security questionnaire draft answers for KMS, audit logging, and data residency
Implement billing integration for burst credits and helper pool usage
Design console tiles for lane UX and real-time handshake visualization
decisions: Ship PRL as an opt-in add-on for Dedicated customers in GA; do not change existing slab SKUs immediately
Helper pool will be preemptible with documented eviction windows (first 6 months); we will offer a non-preemptible helper only for Gold SLA at +20% price
Burst handshake allowed between lanes under same customer account and region only (no cross-region borrowing initially)
Burst credits will be consumable at a tiered premium to baseline token price; credits expire quarterly unless rolled into a renewal discount
tradeoffs: Complexity vs flexibility: PRL adds SKU complexity for Sales/Billing; we mitigate with a simple default 3-pack offering
Predictability vs capacity utilization: handshake increases utilization but reduces isolation guarantees; addressed via handshake caps and eviction policies
Legal appetite: contractual complexity for burst needs prescriptive SLAs; will use a short addendum instead of reworking master agreement
risks: Billing correctness risk on credit accounting (high) — dependency ENG-57421 for reconciliation
Sales enablement friction if SKUs too granular (medium)
Customer confusion around preemptible helper behaviour (medium)
Operational risk of handshake thrashing causing noisy neighbor p99 impacts (high)
mitigations: Run closed pilot with two customers and strict telem thresholds before GA
Limit handshake to 20% per donor lane and 10-minute continuous window for first 90 days
Add automatic fallback to baseline model variant after repeated handshake failures
Implement billing integration tests and reconciliation job prior to customer billing cycle
pilot_plan: Q2 pilot: onboard Nimbus AI and HelixSearch with 3-month pilots
Collect metrics: conversion lift, churn risk, average burst credit burn per tenant, p99 latency during handshake events
Run weekly review with Eng, Sales, Legal, and Security; go/no-go decision at week 10
security_qna_changes: KMS: Offer customer-managed KMS for private deployments; document key rotation policy and HSM usage
Audit logs: lane-level handshake events must be logged to tenant audit stream with retention controls
Data residency: lanes are region-scoped and cannot borrow cross-region; record this in security addendum
SOC2 / ISO: Add PRL to scope for SOC2 next attestation cycle; update control matrix
legal_feedback: Need explicit language for 'best-effort' helper pool and scenario examples for preemption to avoid ambiguous obligations
Recommend quarterly credit expiration language and an option to convert to renewal discount — legal will draft template addendum
sales_feedback: Prefer 3 canned packages (Starter 2-lane, Growth 4-lane, Enterprise customizable) over full SKU menu
Ask for an easy-to-run ROI calculator in sales pack; created a sample sheet in Drive
engineering_feedback: ENG-55123: Core quota refactor required to represent lane granularity; estimate 3 sprints
ENG-57421: Billing reconciliation job needed; flagged for P0 in Q2 sprint planning
Feature flags required for handshake and helper pool; recommend start with handshake=false default
design_feedback: DES-3390: Console should expose lane ownership and a compact handshake timeline; initial mockups attached to ticket
Request for in-console 'explain burst' microcopy to reduce support tickets
metrics_and_success: Primary: Conversion rate from trial to paid for dedicated offers (+target +12% vs control)
Secondary: Average monthly burst credit burn per tenant (target <10% of committed spend)
Reliability SLO: p99 latency uplift during handshake events <10% from baseline
Ops: Billing reconciliation mismatch rate <0.1% per billing cycle
next_steps: Lock SKU pricing and publish internal PRD by 2026-03-20
Legal to produce draft addendum by 2026-03-27
Spin up ENG implementation epics (ENG-55123 / ENG-57421) and schedule design sprint
Identify pilot customers and sign MOU for Q2 pilots
